problem: FIDELITY / THEOLOGY. Neither verse says the babes asked; Matthew 11:25 says the Father hid and revealed. Making the asking the cause of the receiving runs the cause-and-effect backward (the response creating the gift) and reads a motive into the wise and prudent the text does not give.
quote: The two agree on where understanding comes from: it is given, and it comes to the one who asks rather than the one who assumes he already has it. The babes receive what the wise cannot reach because the babes asked and the wise did not think they needed to.
fix: The two agree on where understanding comes from: it is given. Solomon asked and it was given him; the babes had nothing in hand and it was revealed to them; the wise and prudent, sure they already had it, were passed over.

problem: VOICE. The closing sentence jabs at the reader ("has not read either verse") instead of naming the system that taught him. The posture is patience toward the person and dismantling of the system.
quote: Whoever thinks the gospel offers rest without a yoke has not read either verse, and whoever thinks the yoke is the Torah as a burden has missed that the rest is found at the end of wearing it.
fix: The pulpit offers a rest with no yoke in it, and the other side of the aisle calls the yoke a burden; both have lost what Sirach and the Messiah say in the same breath, that the rest is found at the end of wearing it.

problem: FIDELITY. The colon makes Ahab's house the one who laid hold on the prophet and bound him; Elijah was never caught. Jezebel sought his life, but the binding is Herod's alone.
quote: Herod did what Ahab's house did: he laid hold on the prophet and bound him, and a queen wanted him dead.
fix: Herod answered the prophet the way Ahab's house had answered Elijah: the king turned on him and a queen wanted him dead; this time the prophet was caught and bound.

problem: THEOLOGY and VOICE. The one who spoke from the bush was the Formed one, not the Formless Father; the framework holds that every spoken appearance of Elohim in the Torah and prophets is the Son. Also "the Elohim of his fathers" carries no parenthetical.
quote: Solomon prays to the Elohim of his fathers who made all things with his word. John says the same of the Word: all things were made by him, and without him was not any thing made that was made (John 1:3). In the fourth watch the disciples see a figure walking on the sea and cry out, and he answers with the words the Formless one gave at the bush: it is I, be not afraid.
fix: Solomon prays to the Elohim (God) of his fathers who made all things with his word. John says the same of the Word: all things were made by him, and without him was not any thing made that was made (John 1:3). In the fourth watch the disciples see a figure walking on the sea and cry out, and he answers with the name the Formed one spoke from the bush: it is I, be not afraid.

problem: FIDELITY. Matthew 14 records a birthday, a dance and an oath; it does not say Herod was drunk. The word is an embellishment the two verses do not carry.
quote: John's beheading in Herod's prison, on the strength of a drunken birthday oath, is exactly the death Wisdom describes.
fix: John's beheading in Herod's prison, on the strength of a rash birthday oath, is exactly the death Wisdom describes.

problem: THEOLOGY. "The food does not cause the defilement" stated flat is the pulpit's reading of Matthew 15 (all foods clean, Leviticus 11 abolished). The matter in the chapter is bread eaten with unwashed hands, a tradition of men; the note should say that so the Torah's clean and unclean stands.
quote: The two verses fence off the same lie from opposite sides: the Father does not cause the falling, and the food does not cause the defilement.
fix: The two verses fence off the same lie from opposite sides: the Father does not cause the falling, and bread eaten with unwashed hands does not cause the defilement.

problem: THEOLOGY. Same risk as 4581: "not the food" without the unwashed-hands context reads as the Torah's food laws set aside. The chapter is about the tradition of the elders, not Leviticus 11.
quote: Put the two together and the source of sin is found — not the Father, not the food, not the unwashed hands, but the heart.
fix: Put the two together and the source of sin is found — not the Father, not the bread, not the unwashed hands the Pharisees fussed over, but the heart.

problem: THEOLOGY. "Nothing the Father made defiles the man" is a blanket principle that overturns Leviticus 11; the Father made the swine and the carrion too, and the Torah calls them unclean. Matthew 15 is about unwashed hands and the tradition of men, and the note already says so a line earlier; the general claim contradicts the Torah the framework holds standing.
quote: Nothing the Father made defiles the man; what defiles him is what his own heart conceives and his mouth lets out, and the good tree bringing forth good fruit in Matthew 7:17 is the same picture.
fix: Bread eaten with unwashed hands does not defile the man; what defiles him is what his own heart conceives and his mouth lets out, and the good tree bringing forth good fruit in Matthew 7:17 is the same picture.

problem: THEOLOGY. Naming the woman of Canaan and then "the limit of his sending" leaves the reader to conclude she stood outside it and was helped as a mercy case. The framework reads her as seed revealed by hearing, one of the lost sheep; the sentence should close that door rather than leave it open.
quote: When the woman of Canaan pressed him, Yahusha (Jesus) named the limit of his sending: the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).
fix: When the woman of Canaan pressed him, Yahusha (Jesus) named the scope of his sending: the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) — and she, who heard the Shepherd and would not be turned away, was one of them.
